Smt Reena Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 May,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:10303
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 9 th Of May, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 12971 of 2025
 Smt Reena Yadav
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Ashish Singh Jadoun - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Saket Udeniya - P.P. for respondent/State.
 With
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 13436 of 2025
 Gagan Parashar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Bal Krishna Sharma - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Saket Udeniya - P.P. for respondent/State.

Order 
1. Since both these applications are arising out of same crime number registered at same police station, therefore, they have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common order.

2. These are first and second applications filed by the applicant - Smt. Reena yadav and applicant - Gagan Parashar respectively under Section 483 of BNSS(439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of bail relating to Crime No.386/2021 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10303 2 MCRC-13436-2025 registered at Police Station Kolaras, District Shivpuri (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 409,
420, 467, 468, 471, 201, 120-B of IPC and Section 13(1)
(a), 13(1) Kha, 13 (2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
3.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for present applicant that Gagan Parashar's first regular bail application was dismissed on 06.01.2025.

Thereafter, Dhansingh Yadav has been granted bail vide Smt Reena Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47105263/
1 order dated 18.03.2025.

entities.text: Smt Reena Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, his second/subsequent bail application has been filed claiming parity with Dhansingh Yadav.
It is also submitted that as per the story of prosecution, in the bank account of Gagan Rs.12 Lacs has been deposited from father Mukesh, Rs.4.36 Lacs from Ravi and Rs.4 Lacs from Salim.
Co-accused persons namely Salim and Ravi have been acquitted by the learned trial Court in this case in another trial.

As against in the bank account of Reena, Mukesh has deposited Rs.3 Lacs, Salim has deposited Rs.2 Lacs and Ravi has deposited Rs.2 Lacs and it is alleged that she has transferred Rs.5 Lacs in the bank account of father Dhan Singh, Rs.9 Lacs to Mahindra and Mahindra Finance Company and Rs.1.27 Lacs cash has been withdrawn, but these facts are not sufficient to implicate them.
The learned trial Court has framed the charges under Sections 406 and 109 of IPC only which is triable by JMFC.
It is also submitted that the co-accused persons Ravi, Saleem and Sunil have also been acquitted by the trial Court in this case.

Remaining co-accused persons Pinki and Pawan have been convicted with the punishment of three years' RI each and Rakesh and Ramesh, employee of the bank have been convicted with the imprisonment of five years each.
The sentence of Pawan and Pinki is suspended by this Court.
It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10303 3 MCRC-13436-2025
also submitted that they are ready to comply with the conditions as imposed by this Court.
Applicants have no criminal history.

4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application on the ground that in the bank account of Gagan Rs.52 Lacs has been deposited which was out of the total amount of Rs.5.8 Crores involved in the incident.
In the bank account of Reena total Rs.32 Lacs of such amount has been deposited.

It is also submitted that present applicants having the knowledge of deposition of such amount, misused the same by transferring it to the other accounts and for purchasing land and shop in respect of which evidence is on record.
Therefore, a clear cut case is made against them qua huge fund of public exchequer in tune to Rs.5.81 crore.

Moreover, the present applicants are not having the parity with co-accused Dhansingh as Dhansingh has been granted bail on the ground that he has not misused the amount deposited in his account and he had no knowledge of such deposition.

Though, this fact is also not correct as entire facts could not be placed before this Court while passing the order of bail in favour of Dhan Singh vide order dated 18.03.2025 and, therefore,
the prosecution moved an application for cancellation of bail against said Dhan Singh.
Hence prays for rejection of the bail application.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. Considering the contentions of the learned counsel, keeping in view the attending facts and circumstances of the case and having specially regard to the amount involved in the incident, finding no parity with the co-accused, this Court is of the considered view that this is not a fit case in which bail NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10303 4 MCRC-13436-2025 may be granted to the present applicants.
7. Consequently, these applications are hereby dismissed.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE Van Smt Reena Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47105263/
